gasolineAReference.meaning: Endpoint reference for estimating an ethanol-content blend; not retail Brazilian gasoline C.

gasolineCRetailReference.note: Reference calculated by volumetric interpolation of gasoline A (AFR 14.7; 0.742 kg/L) and anhydrous ethanol (AFR 9.0; 0.789 kg/L). Not a lab analysis of fuel from a specific station.

hydrousEthanolReference.note: Proxy based on literature properties for 95 vol% ethanol plus 5 vol% water; Brazilian pump hydrous ethanol can vary within specification and requires fill-up calibration.

fuelProperties.unknownFlexReferenceMeaning: Reference E50 estimate by volume, not a measurement of the tank composition.
fuelProperties.blendCalculation: Density is volume-weighted. Stoichiometric AFR is mass-weighted: sum(volumeFraction * density * AFR) / blendDensity.

requirements: Three or more full-to-full intervals using the same fill endpoint and fuel selection.
Estimated liters must be integrated from fresh, valid fuel-rate samples, not cached display values.
Reject outliers outside the configured factor envelope rather than learning from them.
Keep separate calibration profiles when the selected fuel changes.
Do not modify historical trips retrospectively without replayable source samples.

researchSources.finding: Prioritizes ECU fuel rate PID 015E, then derives flow from MAF; also documents speed-density MAP/IAT/RPM estimation.
Documents MAF-derived fuel economy and MAP/IAT/RPM speed-density estimation; recommends fill-up data to calibrate volumetric efficiency.
As of the research date, gasoline C common is temporarily E32 from 2026-08-01 for 180 days; model parameters have an explicit review date.
Reports density and stoichiometric AFR varying with ethanol/water ratio; 95 vol% ethanol with 5% water is used only as a proxy.
